title: Scenario
description: Frontmatter contract for a multi-model scenario README. A scenario combines two or more model releases in one walkthrough, so it cannot live in a single capsule. It need not be a comparison — a publisher-scoped scenario is often a deeper technical dive that uses several of that publisher's models together. Publisher-scoped scenarios live at models/<publisher>/multi-model-scenarios/<slug>/; cross-publisher scenarios live at models/multi-model-scenarios/<slug>/.

slug.description: Kebab-case folder slug — matches the scenario folder name.

summary.description: Short phrase describing what this release lets you do, e.g. "Generate and edit images from text prompts". Used verbatim in the repo README table, CAPSULE-TOC.md, catalog.json, and llms.txt - every one of which shows the scenario title right next to it, so do not repeat the title or "on Microsoft Foundry" here. No trailing period; llms.txt adds one where it needs a full sentence.

last_updated.description: Date this artifact was added or last meaningfully revised (ISO). Drives the ordering and the 'Last updated' column in CAPSULE-TOC.md. Defaults to release_date for capsules when omitted. Kept in frontmatter rather than read from git so a shallow CI checkout produces identical output.

scope.description: 'publisher' when every model comes from one publisher, going deeper on that publisher's lineup (models/<publisher>/multi-model-scenarios/<slug>/); 'cross-publisher' when the scenario spans publishers (models/multi-model-scenarios/<slug>/). The scope must match the folder the scenario lives in.

publisher.description: Publisher slug. Required when scope is 'publisher'; omit for cross-publisher scenarios.

models.description: The releases this scenario combines. Two or more — a single-model walkthrough belongs in that model's capsule instead.

publisher.description: Publisher slug — must match a folder under models/.

model.description: Model slug — must match a capsule folder under models/<publisher>/.

role.description: What this model contributes to the scenario.

capabilities.description: Capability tags exercised by the scenario. Same enum as capsules — every tag needs a docs/primers/<slug>.md.

dependencies.description: Scenario-specific Python deps appended to requirements-dev.txt.

notebooks.description: Notebooks shipped with this scenario (paths relative to the scenario folder, at folder root). Each notebook covers 1–3 concepts; split rather than grow one.
